{"review_summary":"All primary safety attack surfaces on 024B-core hold. Cascade-status fail-closed default fires for absent, unrecognised, and multi-valued inputs; the exactly-one-cascade-status and exactly-one-Target assertions close multi-occurrence injection and phantom-target attacks. Path-traversal denylist is checked on the readlink-f resolved path, correctly catching /private/var/* macOS symlink canonicalisation before the case-pattern match. Bootstrap-only guard (exit 1) fires at lines 50-52 before the SHA non-existence check (exit 2) at line 152. Adopter-slug canonicalization correctly converts jrnb2024/repo.foo_bar → jrnb2024-repo-foo-bar (._ both replaced). Template workflow-level permissions are contents:read + statuses:write only; no id-token: or attestations:. Fork-PR refusal if: clause is present and covered by assert_wrapper_contract. The blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative log-file assertion fires correctly. File-path containment for --dispatch-note, --status-md, and --branch-protection-log uses realpath and REPO_ROOT prefix check. Phantom-log-injection via other-file is closed: gh pr diff and git diff both filter to the log file path only. D-044 trust-model claims accurately describe the implementation. Three minor findings surface: a 7-char SHA prefix that silently suppresses the TF-023E-002 safety warning if it becomes ambiguous; a TOCTOU window between denylist check and mkdir/write calls; and the --allow-not-applicable flag having no runtime enforcement beyond documentation — any caller can pass it to exit 0 on a cascade-status: not applicable slice with no onboarding checks. One nit: test cleanup trap asymmetry.", "findings": [{"id": "SB-001", "severity": "MIN", "claim": "V1_2_0_SHA_PREFIX='5d4341b' (scaffold-downstream.sh:17) is a 7-char abbreviation. If the SCP repo gains another commit sharing this prefix, git rev-parse --verify exits non-zero, the || true swallows the error, V1_2_0_CUTOVER_SHA becomes empty, and the TF-023E-002 post-v1.2.0 safety warning is silently suppressed for ALL affected SHAs without any diagnostic.", "evidence": "scaffold-downstream.sh:17 (V1_2_0_SHA_PREFIX), lines 155-160 (git rev-parse --verify --quiet ... || true; if [ -n \"$V1_2_0_CUTOVER_SHA\" ]). test_scaffold_downstream.sh lines 178-218: missing-cutover repo test validates exit 0 with no warning when V1_2_0_CUTOVER_SHA is empty, confirming the silent-skip path.", "impact": "Operator emits a post-v1.2.0 wrapper without the expected TF-023E-002 warning; the wrapper will fail GitHub Actions startup at the attest-scorecard job permissions ceiling without operator awareness or a recommended SHA to fall back to.", "mitigation": "Replace V1_2_0_SHA_PREFIX with the full 40-char commit SHA, or emit warn() when V1_2_0_CUTOVER_SHA is empty AND SCP_SHA != V1_0_0_SCP_SHA so ambiguity is distinguishable from a legitimate fresh-repo environment."}, {"id": "SB-002", "severity": "MIN", "claim": "TOCTOU exists between the readlink-f denylist check (scaffold-downstream.sh:135-148) and the mkdir-p/sed write calls (lines 170-181). The denylist is checked on the resolved path string; if OUTPUT_DIR's directory is atomically replaced with a symlink to a system path between check and write, mkdir-p follows the new symlink, bypassing the denylist.", "evidence": "scaffold-downstream.sh:135-138 (OUTPUT_DIR resolved to string), 144-148 (denylist case check on resolved string), 170 (mkdir -p \"$WORKFLOWS_DIR\"), 181 (sed writes wrapper). No post-mkdir re-verification of the resolved path exists. Bootstrap-only design is the primary mitigation; no atomic check-and-create.", "impact": "On a multi-user system, a race-winning attacker could redirect scaffolder output to a system path. Practical risk is low: script is bootstrap-only (no CI), runs as non-root, and the attacker needs write access to OUTPUT_DIR's parent. Blast radius limited to files the operator could write anyway.", "mitigation": "After mkdir -p, re-verify that realpath of WORKFLOWS_DIR still satisfies the denylist (or begins with the expected OUTPUT_DIR prefix) before writing. Alternatively, use Python's os.makedirs + open with O_CREAT and O_NOFOLLOW flags to reject symlinks at write time."}, {"id": "SB-003", "severity": "MIN", "claim": "--allow-not-applicable flag in check-invocation-log-entry.sh bypasses ALL cascade enforcement (no log-entry check, no target-match, no TF-reference check) when cascade-status is 'not applicable'. No runtime guard verifies the caller is a tooling slice; the gate is documentation-only. A cohort slice (024C/D/E/F) that declares 'cascade-status: not applicable' and whose invocation includes --allow-not-applicable silently exits 0 with no onboarding record.", "evidence": "check-invocation-log-entry.sh:168-175 (not-applicable branch exits 0 with only ALLOW_NOT_APPLICABLE=1 check). D-044: 'explicit tooling-slice opt-in gate... operator-responsibility carve-out per plan-doc §2'. No env check (CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS), no file-signature proof, no second confirmation flag prevents misuse.", "impact": "A cohort cascade slice could merge with no invocation-log entry, no target verification, and no TF-reference validation if the flag is passed (inadvertently or deliberately). The only defense is the operator reading the documentation. Technical safeguard is absent until 024B-extras workflow wiring gates the flag to tooling-only contexts.", "mitigation": "Emit a visible warn() to stderr when --allow-not-applicable is accepted (so CI logs show an auditable signal). Optionally require a second explicit opt-in flag such as --confirm-tooling-slice to reduce accidental misuse surface without adding full machine-detectable slice-type logic."}, {"id": "SB-004", "severity": "nit", "claim": "test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh line 12 uses 'trap cleanup EXIT' but omits INT and TERM signals. The CI enforcement test's TMPDIR is in system /tmp (not repo-local), so residue on kill lands in shared temp space.", "impact": "Residual temp dirs in /tmp on interrupted test runs. Low severity; no security bypass. Inconsistent with the scaffolder test harness pattern and may leave test case git repos and fake-gh scripts in /tmp.", "mitigation": "Change 'trap cleanup EXIT' to 'trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM' to match the scaffolder test pattern."}]}
